Never pull the trigger with something that cannot shoot anybody: camera, toolgun, physgun, melee, or a weapon with no ammo concept. Per player: the angle the FOV gate measured against its threshold (green = passed), the same angle from the camera, and where the player sits on the drawn ellipse (1.00 = on the edge).  Green but still no shot means FOV is not what refuses the target.
REQUIRED: Offsetting angles avoids immediate ban from angle-consistency check.
CRITICAL: If disabled, cheating/silent angles will NOT match real mouse inputs, causing a 100% ban for Viewangle Manipulation!
RECOMMENDED: Prevents autoshooting during rapid snaps to avoid detection by snap checks.

CRITICAL: LSAC flags a tick delta of 0 or above 3 between two consecutive commands while holding fire. This walks into the shift inside that band instead of jumping, so backtrack keeps working; unavoidable jumps are rate-limited to one per 3s.
CRITICAL: If disabled, clicking at identical intervals will trigger a 100% ban for Autofire Timed Checks!
Paces autofire/autoshoot by game time (not frames) so Nova autoclick checks do not flag it. Needs Anti-AC on; if off, high FPS can cause detection.

Keeps opt-in game-event subscriptions off the wire. Only Loggers > DamageLogs > "Subscribe to player_hurt event" uses one today: it sets a bit in clc_ListenEvents, which LSAC's sourcenet can majority-vote across players. Off = the subscription is allowed while Anti-AC stays on.

Both walk the model's hitbox set: one visibility trace per hitbox per target, per tick. Ordered takes the highest-priority visible hitbox (head first); Closest takes the visible one nearest your crosshair. Use the popup to trim the cost on a wide FOV.
Remembers each aim point's visibility for the current tick, so the same point is not traced again by another backtrack record, the ESP pass or the close-range head retry.
The two extra head points (for heads peeking cover) cost two traces per target. ON = only within 800 units, where they actually help.

Keeps a target whose direct ray is blocked when the weapon pack's own penetration maths says the bullet still arrives.  Supported packs: ArcCW, ARC9, TacRP, SWCS, TFA (incl. Insurgency), M9K, CW 2.0, SWB (incl. the UT fork), FA:S 2.0. Each one is modelled separately - budgets, material tables and damage loss are that pack's own numbers, not a shared guess.  Silent on a pack with no wallbang, and on a server that has turned its pack's penetration convar off.  Homigrad/Z-City has its own, older autowall with its own switch under Compensation > Gamemode support - that pack ricochets and fires from the world model's muzzle, so it needs its own simulator.

Damage that has to survive the cover before the shot is worth taking. A round that arrives with nothing left only gives your position away.  Ignored on a weapon whose damage could not be read - an unknown number is not a reason to refuse a shot the maths says lands.

How many surfaces the bullet may cross.  Each wall is a long trace plus an exit search, run per aim point per target - 1 is the honest default. CW 2.0, SWB and FA:S allow exactly one and cap this themselves; SWCS allows four, ARC9 three, TFA whatever its weapon says.

The server rewinds PLAYERS when it traces your bullet, and nothing else. A body that is not a player - the prop_ragdoll a downed Homigrad player actually is, or an NPC - is hit where it stands NOW, while you aim where it was drawn: cl_interp + ping ago. Moving bodies miss, still ones do not.  On = shift the aim point by that body's measured velocity. Players are never touched, so backtrack keeps working as it does today.
Ceiling on the shift, in units. A tumbling ragdoll stops being described by a straight line past some magnitude - this makes it under-lead instead of walking the aim point off the body.
Which hitboxes the aimbot may shoot. Click entries to tick them, the list stays open.

Classic (lock): for SetEyeAngles-recoil packs (M9K etc.) - freezes   the view for 4 ticks after each shot so the kick never happens.   Undetectable (zero angle delta), but the mouse stiffens briefly   while firing, and view-punch packs are not covered. Rage: both recoil families, live mouse, no screen movement.   Kills the SetEyeAngles kick by dropping view writes that come   from inside prediction (the mouse never writes from there), and   compensates the view punch on the sent angles while you hold   fire, so ARC9/HL2-style bullets land on the crosshair.
Keep the visual kick on screen while the bullets stay compensated. Looks like a legit player pulling down - for OBS/spectating admins.

LSAC servers only: drops IN_ATTACK on 1-3 cooldown ticks per shot so the Eye Sync forcing re-anchors to our angles instead of letting the spray climb. Costs attack edges (~fire rate, randomized) and does nothing while ADS (IN_ATTACK2) is held.

Marks every stored record (each backtrackable position). Purely visual - turning it off changes nothing about the aim. Also covers the records HVH lag comp stores.  Style picks what a record is drawn AS; see the tooltip there.

Dots  - a marker at each record's eye. Says where and how many, reads at a glance, hides nothing. Chams - each record drawn in the POSE the server would restore. Says what a shot solved against it would actually hit, which is the view that answers 'why did that miss'. One full model draw per pose. Both  - the dot marks the record its pose belongs to.
Hide records outside the server's acceptance band. Those are poses it will never rewind to, so drawing one claims a shot that cannot happen.  Off shows the whole stored history, shootable or not.

Writes cl_extrapolate 0 straight onto the ConVar (it is a cheat cvar, so the console cannot set it on a normal server).  When the connection starves, the engine runs EVERY entity up to 0.25s past its last real position - a pose the server never had, so both the live aim and the records taken then are fiction. With this on it clamps to the last real snapshot instead.  Costs a visible stutter during packet loss. Does NOT affect fakelaggers: the engine already clamps a player whose updates stopped while other packets keep arriving. Restored on disconnect and on unload.

Acknowledges an OLDER server packet than the one you really got, so the server measures a bigger round trip and widens its lag-compensation window by exactly that much.  Nothing you send is delayed - there is no input lag. The cost is that your ping is genuinely higher to everyone, scoreboard included.  Remote servers only: a listen server has no latency to inflate.

TOTAL latency the server should measure, real ping included. The cap is 890 and not 1000 because the server prunes its history at sv_maxunlag (1.0s) and the pose it must still find sits at this plus your interp.

Rewind depth is your ping + this + interp, and sv_maxunlag caps the SUM. Past the cap the depth stops growing but the acceptance band keeps climbing, so every usable record ends up jammed against the oldest edge of the history -- exactly the poses the server is dropping. That reads as 'backtrack misses'.  The request is clamped here rather than sent, so this costs you no extra real ping either. Lower the slider to make the line go away.
Never acknowledge across a reliable-state change. Costs a little depth right after chat/kill traffic. Leave on unless you are debugging.
Also rewinds the reliable flip-flop. Ages the ack clock harder, but the server then RETRANSMITS reliable traffic - chat, kill feed and joins arrive twice. Off by default.

Simulates your next movement tick locally so the aimbot leads with the origin you are about to have. It runs with the gamemode's Lua hooks off, so GM:SetupMove / GM:Move never see it.  Turn OFF on gamemodes that restrict movement from Lua - handcuffs, stuns, cutscene locks. There the sim moves you when the server does not: you walk while cuffed and then rubber-band back.  No spread is not affected either way.
Support for the Z-City / Homigrad weapon pack. Set No visual recoil to Classic on this pack.
Comma-separated weapon bases using the Homigrad method contract. Applies on every server.
Kills what moves your aim. Needs No spread on.
Kills what shakes the screen. Needs No visual recoil on.
A downed player is a parked dot; the body is a separate ragdoll. Aim at the body.

Reverts the whole Z-City aim path to build 16 (10.08) in one switch: no per-tick muzzle sample, no shot feedback loop, no walk lead, the old 14 deg solver ceiling, the raw view basis, no bullet-redirect detection, and the pack's norecoil flag written unconditionally. Also restores the unconditional CreateMove angle restore that 7b2bccf made conditional.  Overrides Pack switch and Bullet redirect while it is on.  For comparing against 16 directly. If 16 comes back, turn the parts below back on one at a time to find which one cost it.
The gun fires along its barrel, not your eye line. Solver also corrects manual shots when Nospread is enabled.

Does nothing while Smooth is 0.  Inside this many degrees the aim stops smoothing and takes the solution in one step.  The last few degrees are where the barrel model's own error lives, and on Z-City the shot is gated on the REAL barrel at the angle being sent - so crawling that stretch does not miss, it holds the trigger for the whole approach.  0 turns it off. Bigger = a larger instant step on acquisition.

Off preserves the pack's shoot animation. Auto also preserves it while Muzzle comp is Solver, and uses the pack flag in other compensation modes.  Always disables the client animation even though the server still runs it; this can make the muzzle model disagree with the server, including on rifles.  Use Auto for the official pose solver.
Auto keeps the barrel ray for the supported Homigrad contract. IsVR alone never changes the ray method. Use Always only for a custom base whose bullet code redirects toward the eye trace.

AutoFire uses a fresh muzzle sample and the aim for this command. Pistol recoil and hand movement already included in the official pose calculation do not need to settle first. Your own clicks are not blocked by this option.

Mode None only, Z-City only. Runs the aim once per tick, the way Silent and PSilent do, instead of once per rendered frame.  The barrel this pack aims by is sampled once a tick, so per frame the aim solves several times against the same sample and steers the view between the steps - that is the crosshair shaking around the head.  Costs: with smoothing on, the crosshair walks at tick rate instead of frame rate.

Stops the crosshair shaking on aim mode None.  The solved angle is written to your real view, that turns the gun, and the gun's new position changes the next solution - a loop that rings at a few Hz and looks like the aimbot is picking random angles around the head.  This holds the barrel correction between ticks and only re-takes it once the gun has stopped moving. Tracking is not slowed: the angle to the target is still rebuilt every frame, only the gun-offset part is held.  Silent and PSilent never move your view, so this does nothing there.
Shoot through thin cover when the bullet still gets there.
Damage that has to survive the walls.
Draw where the bullet goes. Needs Muzzle comp = Solver.
Damage at the impact, and walls/bounces taken.

Octothorp pack - Dobrograd and the other OctoTeam DarkRP servers. Off = we never touch its trigger gate or its muzzle geometry. The cone itself comes from the weapon backend either way, because this pack calls FireBullets on the SERVER only.

The pack's CanFire() refuses unless the server has set its IsReady netvar, which needs right-click held (or crouch, with a long gun). Without this, autoshoot/triggerbot press the trigger of a weapon that has already decided not to fire. Auto: hold right-click while the aimbot has a target. (default) Always: hold it whenever an octo gun is out. Off: never touch it - you aim down sights yourself.
Aim from the weapon barrel, including its position and direction. Works without nospread. Solver is the default. Old Angle profiles use Solver automatically.
Smooth camera motion relative to your view. Turning and walking keep their normal response. The sight transition is smoothed too. Bullet aim is unchanged.

Runs BESIDE the legit aimbot, reusing its target selection, backtrack records, visibility and resolver -- only the policy differs: no smoothing, no FOV cone, the angle is written on the tick it exists.  This is loud. It is meant to be.
Held, not toggled. Unbound (0) means always on while enabled.

Pull the trigger whenever the weapon backend reports ready. There is no hitchance gate: with Nospread on the cone is no longer random, so a 'chance' would be gating on a number that stopped describing anything.
Write the angle into the command only. Off also moves your actual view, which is visible to you and to spectators.

For targets the server refuses to rewind (fake laggers). Carries them forward through the real movement code, in steps of their own command bundle, to a pose the server is actually holding. Falls back to cl_lagcompensation 0, which the server can see.

Turns aimbot_settings.anti_lsac OFF while rage is held and puts YOUR value back the moment it is not -- the angle-delta limiter, the reversal check, the fake mouse deltas and the movement octant snap all hang off that one master.  Every one of them exists to make the aim look like a hand, and every one costs accuracy. In a rage fight the anti-aim has already given that away.
Backwards, flipped left/right once per server update, so their aim lands where you were one update ago.
Choked commands steer the server's body, the sent one shows enemies the far side of it. Holds ~170 deg at any choke depth. NEEDS FAKE LAG -- with nothing choked it is just Backwards.
Which way the body is turned. The server's hitboxes follow the FEET, so this decides whether the anti-aim does anything at all. Alternate flips every ~0.18s. Freestanding overrides it.
Pick the side from cover instead of alternating: the body turns toward the closer wall. Does nothing in the open.
Layered on top of the direction instead of replacing it, so 'backwards + jitter' is reachable. Steps once per server update.
What 'backwards' and 'sideways' are measured from. Your own view means backwards points at anyone you are not looking at.
Hold a side on a key instead of letting it alternate.
Press again to release. Back is ignored by Real desync (it already faces away).
Arrows at the crosshair. The lit one is the body side, not the key.

Anti-aim normally stops on every tick you hold fire. This keeps it steering on the ticks the weapon is still on cooldown. Only works on weapons with an engine fire clock -- the log line [AA-COOLDOWN] says whether it is doing anything.
(!) Fake Lag is OFF -- LBY modes need it
Silent: your own view is untouched.
Replays the enemy's animation for several guesses at the commands we never received. Does nothing to a MOVING enemy -- the engine pins his feet to his eyes, so there is nothing to resolve.
Never touches the yaw, only flattens a fake pitch. The safe choice on servers full of legit players.

Sample six points around each head/chest/stomach box instead of trusting the centre and two diagonals.  THE CASE IT FIXES: the head is the chosen group and an arm is in front of it. With three samples all three trace into the arm, the head is called invisible, and the aimbot drops a group and shoots the ARM. A head box is a few units across and a limb rarely covers all of it -- this finds the exposed sliver and keeps the head.  Costs traces only when nothing on the preferred group is visible yet: the scan still stops at the first point it can see, and the centre stays first because it is the most forgiving of a wrong resolve.  With Multi-hypothesis points also on, these extra samples are ordered by how many resolver guesses contain them -- that is the real safe point: one that hits whichever guess turns out right.
Build a skeleton per guess and prefer aim points that hit under the most of them. Live targets only, not backtrack records.

How far the six samples sit from the box centre, as a percentage of its half-size.  Low = huddled near the centre: safest against a wrong resolve, but finds fewer exposed slivers. High = out at the faces: finds the peeking edge, but a point near the face leaves the box the moment the resolve is off. 70%% is the compromise.
How many guesses to build. Each one costs a bone setup.
Start the search at directions taken from the target (last hit, movement heading, goal feet yaw) instead of a blind table.

Do not move the search on an outcome that says nothing about the yaw.  Two cases, both measurable rather than guessed:   * every hypothesis covered the aim point -- they all predict the SAME     outcome, so a miss was not caused by the yaw and a hit does not name     a winner (needs Multi-hypothesis points);   * the target crouched mid-flight -- duck is predicted for you and only     interpolated for him, so that pose was never the server's.  The search gets ONE scored shot per round trip. Spending those on misses the yaw did not cause walks it away from the right angle exactly as fast as it walks toward it. Off = the old behaviour, charge everything.
Enemy sends pitch +-89 to tilt his whole skeleton. This flattens it to 0 before the hitboxes are built.
Turning the legs alone leaves the chest and head at the twist the client guessed. This sets the twist the server holds. Leave on.
Experimental: hook the animation state and let the engine rebuild the pose instead of rotating it. Mostly covered by Torso twist now.
Per-enemy state next to each player: AA/legit verdict, choke, deg/tick, current guess, misses and hits.
Where hit/miss comes from. The exact source needs "Subscribe to player_hurt event" under Loggers > DamageLogs.
Master switch for desync visualization. Use ... to configure lines and fake chams separately.
ESP-projected direction lines. Excluded from GTS and streamproof clean captures.

Builds your third-person body at the yaw the SERVER is holding, so what you see is what an enemy's hitboxes are doing. The engine builds the pose, so the torso twist and the limbs are the server's.  Off falls back to Fake chams, which rotates an already-built pose rigidly -- that is why the red copy looks stretched and bent. Visual only: the server is driven by the command angles, which this never touches.
Ghost is off while the model is rebuilt.
On-screen readout of your own feet yaw (current / goal / delta). Use it to confirm the animstate layout reads correctly in-game.

Phase-0 measurement, debug only. Host a listen server or start a map, turn this on, choke a few ticks, then turn it off and read the VERDICT line in the log. Does nothing at all when server.dll is not in this process.
Fine-tune the sent tick_count if hits land just ahead/behind the enemy. 0 = auto (ping+interp). Raise if shots hit where they WERE, lower if ahead.
Keep drawing players the server has stopped transmitting. Their box freezes where they were last seen.

How far the dormant reveal reaches. 0 = unlimited. The stalest boxes are the far ones: a low value keeps the ghost of someone who just went round a corner, and drops the half-server a transmit optimizer dropped.

Paint dormant players - box, skeleton and every text - with the color below, so a stale box is never mistaken for a live one. Wins over Team / Usergroup / Friend colors, loses to the aim target.  Works on any dormant player on screen, including ones held by the grace window, not only the ones this toggle reveals.

Show players hidden via NODRAW / ShouldDraw=false (hoverboard riders, cloak SWEPs, some seats, distance-fog addons), and put their MODEL back into the render - chams/glow work on them again.  Cannot help with dormant players: the engine refuses to draw what the server is not transmitting.
Hide boxes on corpses. Chams, glow, look beams and the aimbot
Highlight the player/NPC you are aiming at or locked onto.

In FOV Candidate - a real aimbot scan (bones, hitscan, visibility traces) once per tick. Exact, but it is the expensive one.  In FOV (fast) - screen-space only: the player whose box is nearest the crosshair inside the FOV circle. Same team/friend/dormant filters, no bone setup and no traces, so it costs almost nothing. It can disagree with the aimbot behind cover or with a hitbox filter.
Paint every ESP text element of the target (name, job, weapon, distance, ...) with the color above. Off by default. Beats a Team / Usergroup / Friend text color, like the box does.
Bone lines over each player (hitbox skeleton).
Line from a screen edge to each player.
All players - unchanged. Aimbot target - one line, to whoever the aimbot / silent aim is on. Inside aimbot FOV - only players within the aimbot FOV circle.
Locked - the player the aimbot is actually aiming at while the aim key is held (silent aim included). FOV candidate - who it WOULD pick right now.
Aimbot is off - no target, no lines.
Arrows at the screen edge pointing to players out of view.
Boxes, bars and texts are arranged in the ESP editor (sidebar) - drag elements straight onto the model there.
Culls every player visual - ESP box, texts, bars, chams, look beams - beyond this distance. 0 = unlimited. Lower it on crowded servers to save FPS.

Material path as the engine sees it: no "materials/" prefix, no ".vmt". Must be a MODEL material (VertexLitGeneric / UnlitGeneric / Refract). World materials (LightmappedGeneric, dev/ grids) render black on players. Enter to apply. Unknown path or empty = Flat.
Changes the skybox client-side (no sv_skyname write). Engine loader = presets + any installed sky, native, works on painted maps. Hidden from OBS / screengrabbers while "Stream-proof view" is on.

Engine = native engine sky loader: presets + any installed sky, no material/loose-file footprint, works on painted/VPK maps. Override = our loose-VMT swap (fallback if the engine signature breaks after a game update).
Which sky the engine loader binds for your view.
Which sky the loose-VMT override points the map's faces at. Nothing of ours is written into materials/ for a preset -- only the six VMTs.
Type any sky already installed in the game, or import your own VTF below.

How often the clean stream frame is re-rendered. Match it to your OBS/record FPS. Lower = cheaper (the heavy 2nd render runs this many times/sec instead of every game frame). This is the main FPS lever: at 30-60 Hz the double-render runs far less often than your game FPS.

Resolution of the clean stream pass, as a %% of your screen (Offscreen mode only). Lower = the 2nd render draws fewer pixels = more FPS if you are GPU/fill-bound, at the cost of a softer stream image (upscaled back to full size for OBS/RSC). 100%% = identical to your screen. Text/HUD in the stream get blurry below ~70%%.  Below 100%% the clean target also gets a size no engine render target shares, which makes the OBS bridge pick it up on the first frame instead of retrying.

We run as a DLL inside the ALREADY RUNNING game, so a .db the process opened at startup can never be deleted from here. What is possible is emptying it through the sqlite connection that already owns it -- every table dropped, every cookie deleted -- for cl.db and mn.db. No Lua is involved: the engine's own sqlite3_exec and its database handle are found by signature, and each connection is asked (PRAGMA database_list) which file it just worked on. sv.db is only open while YOU host, so it is deleted outright.  GMod's sqlite is built with SQLITE_OMIT_VACUUM: DROP TABLE leaves the old bytes in the freed pages. The wipe therefore refills the freelist with junk until PRAGMA freelist_count hits 0. Reclaiming the SPACE still needs the game closed. A .db is never truncated -- a zeroed file under a live sqlite handle is a corrupt database, not a clean one.

cl_timeout back to 30 (a banned client gets a secret value stored in it) plus net_graph / developer / cl_showpos to 0. Written natively, so a Lua RunConsoleCommand override never sees it. Applied on the next tick in-game.

Randomises the modification time of exactly the four paths the fingerprint hashes:   garrysmod/gameinfo.txt   garrysmod/lua/autorun/base_vehicles.lua   garrysmod/lights.rad   <root>/sourceengine (the folder itself) They are the only part of a device fingerprint the client actually controls.

Also ages every loose file in the game root (what file.Find("*", "base_path") returns) back by months, so "fresh install" / "reinstall" checks -- oldest file newer than 1-2 days -- stop firing after a re-download.
Everything off by default. A file the game holds open cannot be deleted -- it gets emptied in place instead (never a .db: those go through the sql wipe).

file.Find("addons/*") is the cheapest scan a server can run, and the listing it returns is a fingerprint of this machine -- every addon you have, every binary module in lua/bin, every leftover in between.  With this on, the paths in the list below answer as if they were not there: gone from listings, and Exists / IsDir / Read / Open / Size / Time answer the way they answer for a path that never existed. The engine is untouched -- everything mounted stays mounted, only what Lua is TOLD changes.  Does not cover require / include: pcall(include, path) is still an existence oracle for a .lua file.

Hidden = does not exist at all. Empty  = the folder is still there, it is just never          holding anything (right for addons/: the          folder is stock, the contents are the tell). *  matches within one folder, ** at any depth: lua/*.lua hides loose Lua files sitting in lua/, lua/**.lua hides every .lua under it.
Nothing cloaked. Add a path below.

Click to switch this path between hidden and empty.

Puts the built-in list back: addons (empty), lua/bin (hidden), lua/*.lua (hidden).  The last one is precise on purpose -- a stock garrysmod/lua holds only directories, so a loose .lua sitting there is always something that was put there (a dump, an executor's scratch file). A broad lua/* would swallow the stock folders instead and make the whole tree vanish, which is far louder than the files it hides.  Replaces the current list, so a config saved with its own rules gets the defaults back only when you press this.

Paths are relative to garrysmod/, and one rule covers every way of spelling the same folder -- "lua/bin" catches all three of file.Find("lua/bin/*","MOD"), file.Find("bin/*","LUA") and file.Find("garrysmod/lua/bin/*","base_path"). Use data/... for the data folder, @root/... for what really is outside garrysmod/ (bin/, sourceengine/, the exe).

Every function carries the name of the file it came from, and debug.getinfo / debug.traceback / jit.util.funcinfo hand it over without touching a single file API. Walk hook.GetTable() and you have a list of what is loaded on this client.  With this on, a function whose file matches a rule above reports as a C function: source "=[C]", short_src "[C]", what "C", line numbers -1 -- all of it together, because half a rewrite is an impossible combination and a sharper tell than the leak.  Chunk names are spelled "lua/<addon-subfolder>/..." or "addons/<name>/...", so the addons rule already covers the second; add lua/<folder> for the first.  Trade-off: an addon of yours that looks up its OWN path this way gets [C] too. Error message text is not covered - only these three functions are.

engine.GetAddons() returns your whole workshop subscription -- title, wsid, size, mounted -- and never goes near the filesystem, so nothing above touches it. Entries whose .gma sits under a cloaked path are dropped.  (!) With the default addons rule that empties the list, and some gamemodes MOUNT CONTENT from it -- wOS dynabase (Z-City/Homigrad) walks GetAddons and calls game.MountGMA(addon.file) for models. Turn this on only if you can live without that.

Reports every game except garrysmod as not installed and not mounted. This is a pure fingerprint input -- nova hashes exactly these flags into its device id.  The list itself is kept, only the flags are cleared: GMod's set of known games is fixed, so an empty list is an anomaly while "owns nothing but the base game" is the commonest setup there is.
